title: The Passion of Steve Jobs
coreMove: Separate an inspiring success story from usable evidence before letting it guide a career decision.
sourcePressure: Steve Jobs and the Stanford advice open Rule 1 by weakening passion-first career folklore without yet replacing it.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating the point as a dunk on Steve Jobs or as proof that love for work never matters.

sourceAnchors.name: Steve Jobs
sourceAnchors.detail: The Stanford transcript freeze supports the 2005 address, find-work-you-love advice, Reed College, calligraphy, Apple, being fired, and later returning.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Steve Jobs sounds clean as a career compass only after the messy route has been edited by success.

sourceAnchors.name: Stanford
sourceAnchors.detail: The address was delivered to Stanford graduates on June 12, 2005 and became a cultural pressure point for passion-first advice.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The Stanford setting matters because the line traveled farther than the evidence beneath it.

worker staring at a resignation letter

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence

exampleSpecs.audience: a graduate applicant comparing a famous curator biography with entry requirements
exampleSpecs.stakes: losing a paid placement by copying a myth instead of reading criteria
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: places the glossy curator profile beside the internship rubric and crosses out every sentence that is admiration rather than evidence
exampleSpecs.firstImage: varnish smell over a half-cleaned frame

exampleSpecs.audience: a data intern tempted by a celebrity general manager origin story
exampleSpecs.stakes: wasting a season chasing narrative instead of proof of skill
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: asks which parts of the famous story would count in a hiring review and writes only those on a whiteboard

exampleSpecs.audience: an assistant stage manager reading a Tony winner profile before touring
exampleSpecs.stakes: mistaking glamour after success for competence-building conditions
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: compares the profile timeline with the call sheet and chooses the job for the reps it gives
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a taped call sheet curling at the corners

exampleSpecs.audience: an advisor helping a student interpret a famous doctor memoir
exampleSpecs.stakes: a student abandoning fieldwork because certainty looks instant
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: sees that the memoir had an ending before she borrowed its lesson
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a returned library copy with sticky notes

exampleSpecs.audience: a junior designer comparing an indie hit interview with her prototype
exampleSpecs.stakes: shipping nothing because the origin story feels magical
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: uses the playtest table to identify ugly builds survived, not love of games, as the usable lesson
exampleSpecs.firstImage: six controllers in a plastic bin

exampleSpecs.audience: an applicant hearing a master tradesperson describe loving the work
exampleSpecs.stakes: missing that affection came after years of competence
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: uses the conduit practice bench to separate love-after-mastery from love-before-entry
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a bent conduit sample on a scratched metal bench

skillTargets: distinguish symbolic force from planning evidence
spot retrospective coherence in success stories
avoid demanding early certainty from thin evidence

tryThisNowSpec: Pick one career story you admire and mark one sentence as inspiration and one sentence as actual evidence you could use today.
